newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities slip despite FOMC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities slip despite FOMC.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options glided lower throughout the day after opening firmer as underlying markets rallied on friendly economic data, dealers said.
Growing expectation the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), due to meet Tuesday and Wednesday, would keep interest rates steady also weighed on volatilities, they added.

"We're really not anticipating much out of the FOMC due to the fact that we saw a lot of the (economic) numbers lately come in a little bit bullish for the market," said a T-bond options trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options slipped to 10.5 percent, unchanged from Friday's depressed pre-weekend level, but well off 10.85 earlier in the day.
T-bonds rallied early on a weaker-than-expected National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index for Janauary. The January NAPM index fell to 52.0 from a revised 53.8 in December.
The rally helped sustain bullish momentum that had been building after last week's rally pushed the market above a declining channel extending from the early December highs, traders said.

While volatilities were generally coming under pressure from growing optimism on the bond market, they were also underpinned, at least for now, by uncertainties on the monthly employment report for January due out on Friday, traders said.
"We're still looking for it (volatility) to come back up this week ahead of the unemployment numbers," the brokerage trader said.
At the shorter end of the curve, front-end volatilities were softer as front-month futures were becoming increasingly stagnant because of the outlook for steady interest rates in the near term.
Implied volatility for June Eurodollar futures options was off a quarter point to 10.8 percent, while September was little changed at 14.0.
There was some sizable put selling, with one firm selling 3,000 contracts of June 94.50 puts and another firm selling 4,000 of June 94.25 puts.
"A lot of people are thinking we have found a level (in futures) where it would be hard to trade back through," an investment bank Eurodollar trader said.
